svg.text: How few distances can n points have? The integer grid {1..m}d, n = md
Exact counts D of distinct distances. The theorem says D is at least cd n2/d for d at least 3; the grid shows the exponent 2/d cannot be raised.
hollow, dashed: n random points of the doubled box {1..2m}d
generic points: every pair distinct, D = n(n-1)/2, far off this scale
60 a sum of 3 squares, but needs a gap above 9
Legendre's theorem removes about 1/6 of the
integers; the box removes more near the top.
Always D is at most 3(m-1)2, below 3 n2/3.
Grid counts: exact sumset of squares, matched by brute-force pair enumeration (d = 2 to 5, n up to 2401) and, on 1 to (m-1)2,
by the two-, three- and four-square theorems. Random subsets seeded (166). Largest grids: n = 27,000,000 (d = 3), 16,777,216 (d = 4).
Illustration of the statement only: grids are the conjectured extremal sets, and no finite computation bears on the lower bound.
